title: Senior's toolkit: the debugging process
summary: Reading diffs, committing small, bisecting a regression, running one test and breaking when an exception is thrown.

steps.title: Senior's toolkit: the debugging process
steps.body: Good debugging is a process, not luck: reproduce it with a test, find the change that caused it, look at the exact moment it breaks, and keep every change small enough to review. These are the commands behind each step.

toolkit.what: Run just the test that reproduces the bug, over and over, while you fix it.
flags: match on the name shown in the results
print every test and what it wrote
skip the build when nothing changed

toolkit.what: See exactly what you changed before you run, commit or ask for review. Most "it worked yesterday" bugs are in this output.
flags: what is staged for the next commit
only file names and line counts
everything your branch changed since it left main

toolkit.what: Stage a change piece by piece, answering y or n for each hunk. It lets you split a messy afternoon into small commits, one idea each.
flags: split the hunk into smaller ones
stop; keep what you staged so far
toolkit.example: git add -p && git commit -m "Fix rounding in Split for three-way shares"

toolkit.what: Binary-search the history for the commit that broke something. 1,000 commits take about 10 test runs.
flags: mark the broken commit and one known to work
let git test each step: exit code 0 means good, 1-127 bad (125 skips)
finish and go back to where you started
toolkit.example:
git bisect start
git bisect bad
git bisect good v1.4.0
git bisect run dotnet test --filter "FullyQualifiedName~SplitTests"
git bisect reset

toolkit.what: Find the commits that added or removed a piece of text: who introduced this line, and why.
flags: commits where the number of occurrences of the text changed

toolkit.what: Make the debugger stop at the line that throws an exception, even if something catches it later. Otherwise you only see where it ended up.
flags: Debug > Windows > Exception Settings (Ctrl+Alt+E), tick Common Language Runtime Exceptions
Run and Debug > Breakpoints > tick All Exceptions

steps.prompt: The invoice-split test passed on the v1.4.0 release and fails on main. There are 300 commits in between and nobody knows which one broke it. What do you type?
options: `git bisect start`, `git bisect bad`, `git bisect good v1.4.0`, then `git bisect run dotnet test --filter "FullyQualifiedName~Split"`
`git log` and read all 300 commit messages
`git diff v1.4.0` and read the whole diff
`git revert HEAD` until the test passes
steps.explain: Bisect halves the range each time, so 300 commits take about 9 test runs, and `run` does them for you. You end with the exact commit and its diff, which usually makes the cause obvious.

steps.prompt: Put the steps of a bisect session in order.
Match each option to its meaning.
pairs: what the next commit will contain
stage one hunk at a time
commits that added or removed the text

steps.prompt: The app logs `InvalidOperationException: Sequence contains no elements`, but the stack trace points into a `catch` block that rethrows a new exception, not to where it started. How do you see the original line?
options: Turn on break-when-thrown for `System.InvalidOperationException` in Exception Settings and run it under the debugger
Add a breakpoint at the top of `Main`
steps.explain: Break when thrown stops at the exact `throw` (here, a `First()` on an empty list) before any handler runs, with all the variables still there.

items: Which of the last 200 commits broke this test?
It worked in the release; when did it stop working?
Who added this magic number, and in which commit?
When did the call to `Math.Floor` disappear?
What exactly have I changed since my last commit?
Which files does my branch touch compared to main?

steps.title: Make it a habit
steps.body: Start every bug by writing the failing test and running only it. Read `git diff` before every commit and keep commits to one idea, so `git bisect` can point at a small change. When the stack trace does not show where it started, switch on break-when-thrown.
